good_tf:
resource "azurerm_container_registry" "example" {
  name                          = "exampleacr12345"
  resource_group_name           = "example-rg"
  location                      = "eastus"
  sku                           = "Standard"
  admin_enabled                 = false
  public_network_access_enabled = false
  anonymous_pull_enabled        = false # FIX: disable anonymous image pulling
}
why_it_matters: Enabling anonymous pull allows unauthenticated users to download container images from the Azure Container Registry over the Docker V2 API.
Exposed container images may contain proprietary source code, hardcoded configuration details, internal endpoint URLs, or software vulnerability details.
Setting anonymous pull to false enforces Azure Active Directory authentication and role-based access control for all image pull requests.
post_en:
Setting anonymous_pull_enabled to true on line 12 is blocking approval for this container registry pull request.

I cannot approve this change as written. Enabling anonymous pull allows unauthenticated clients to pull container images directly from our registry over the Docker V2 API without presenting credentials.

Our application images contain compiled code, dependency layers, and internal service architecture details. Exposing these artifacts publicly removes all identity controls and audit logging for image pull activity.

Please set anonymous_pull_enabled to false to enforce authentication on all image read operations.

CKV_AZURE_138 flags this exposed registry attribute automatically during automated Terraform scanning.

Container registries must require explicit authentication for all image read requests to prevent public artifact retrieval.
